bull: Profit per share jumped to $4.23 last quarter from $1.88 a year earlier, because oil prices are still far above where they were a year ago.

bear: Brent oil fell to about $92 a barrel on November 16 after trading as high as $120 during the Iran conflict, and lower oil means less profit per barrel.

Because the Dow holds only 30 companies, one big drop pulls the whole average much harder; health insurers earn much of their money from government health plans, so new rules on those payments can shrink their profits.

watch.what: Walmart earnings: strong sales would show shoppers are fine and help the Dow; weak sales would add to the slide.
Fed decision: a quarter-point hike is expected; a half-point hike would be a bigger hit.

briefs.name: Russell 2000
briefs.headline: Russell 2000 edges up 0.46% as rates and oil slip
briefs.summary: The Fed held its key rate at 3.75% to 4% on October 28, but two officials, Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack, voted to raise it. The Fed raised rates in September for the first time in more than three years. Target, Lowe's and TJX all reported results that beat or pleased investors on Wednesday.
bull: The 10-year rate eased to about 5.07%, a small break on borrowing costs, which matter more for small companies.
US oil fell 3.04% to $82.08, lowering fuel costs for small businesses like truckers and restaurants.
Target and Lowe's beat forecasts, and small companies earn most of their money inside the US, so steady shoppers help them.
bear: Fed official Christopher Waller said a half-point hike may be needed in December, and rate traders already fully expect at least a quarter-point hike.
Pending home sales fell 4.7% in October to the lowest since at least 2001, bad for small builders and home-related firms.
Waller said inflation is 'headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out', which could mean more hikes after December.
briefs.nextEvent: Fed interest rate decision on Wednesday, December 9, 2026

briefs.about: The Russell 2000 tracks about 2,000 smaller US companies. It shows how smaller businesses, which often depend more on loans and the US economy, are doing.
briefs.whyMoved: The Russell 2000 rose 0.46%, or 12.44 points, on Wednesday to 2,714.31, a small bounce after Tuesday's close of 2,701.87, its lowest in two weeks; it was 2,856.95 on November 4, so smaller companies are still down about 5% since then. It gained on a day when the 10-year rate slipped to about 5.07% and US oil fell 3% to $82.08, while the Dow fell 1.11%. Smaller companies borrow more of their money, often at rates that change, so even a small dip in rates helps their profits, while a Fed hike would hurt them most.

watch.what: Fed decision: a quarter-point hike is expected; a half-point hike would hit small companies hardest, while a softer message could lift them.

briefs.headline: Micron jumps about 4.7% after hours as Nvidia's huge quarter eases AI fears
briefs.about: Micron makes memory chips, the parts that store data in computers, phones and the giant data centers that run AI. Its main products are DRAM and NAND flash memory, plus HBM, a fast memory built for AI chips.
briefs.summary: On November 16, the US Commerce Department made companies get licenses to send advanced AI chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, to stop chips from slipping into China. Micron is one of seven companies, along with Google, Nvidia and AMD, buying part of a $26 billion block of Anthropic shares at its IPO price, with Micron's share reported at $1.0 billion. Before Tuesday, Micron had dropped 18.7% from its $884.74 close on October 30, partly on worries that it plans to spend more than $25 billion on new factories.
bull: Nvidia raised its growth forecast for its next fiscal year to 75% from 70%, and every Nvidia AI system needs lots of memory, so more Nvidia sales usually mean more Micron sales.
Micron made $84.97 billion of profit on $133.19 billion of sales in its last year, so it keeps about 64 cents of each sales dollar as profit.
Analysts' average 12-month price goal is about $1,624, more than double Tuesday's $712.42 close, with DA Davidson's $3,000 the highest.
bear: Nvidia's forecast assumes zero AI chip sales to China, and the new November 16 license rule could slow AI chip sales in five more countries, which means less memory needed.
A judge has let a lawsuit move ahead that says memory makers worked together to keep DRAM prices high, which could lead to costly penalties.
Nvidia expects its profit margin to shrink to 71% to 72% from 74.9%, and higher memory prices are one cost that big customers may push back on.
briefs.nextEvent: Micron's next quarterly report, expected around December 16, 2026

briefs.name: Micron Technology
briefs.whyMoved: Micron fell 7.62% on Monday, November 16, to $719.02, then slipped another 0.92% to $712.42 on Tuesday after being down 5.47% in the morning, leaving it about 8.5% below its $778.31 close on November 13. After Tuesday's close, Nvidia, Micron's biggest buyer of HBM memory for AI chips, reported $115.84 billion in quarterly sales, about $6.7 billion more than expected, and said next quarter could reach about $130 billion. Micron then rose about 4.7% to roughly $745.80 in after-hours trading. Almost all of Micron's giant profit now comes from AI data centers, and Nvidia said its new Vera Rubin systems, which hold more memory each, are off to an 'explosive start', so Nvidia's growth is a direct signal for Micron's memory orders.

watch.what: Anthropic's stock starts trading and Samsung and SK Hynix news comes out in Korea. A strong Anthropic debut would show money still pouring into AI; a weak one could hurt memory stocks.
Micron's expected quarterly report (estimated date). Good: a higher sales forecast and steady memory prices. Bad: a lower forecast or signs AI customers are slowing orders.

market.why: On Wednesday, November 18, stocks were mixed: the Dow fell 561 points as health insurer UnitedHealth dropped about 6% on a new government anti-fraud plan, and Nvidia slid 2.9% even after sales jumped 103%. Fed official Christopher Waller said a big half-point rate hike may be needed in December, which worried traders. Tech in the Nasdaq and smaller Russell 2000 companies still edged up as investors got ready for Anthropic's stock debut on Thursday.
